first: अधमा धनमिइच्छन्ति धनं मानं च मध्यमाः ।
en: The lowest people want only wealth, middling people want wealth and honour, and the best want honour alone; honour is the wealth of the great.

first: इक्षुरापः पयो मूलं ताम्बूलं फलमौषधम् ।
en: Even after eating sugarcane, water, milk, roots, betel leaf, fruit or medicine, one may still bathe, give gifts and do other sacred duties.

first: दीपो भक्षयते ध्वान्तं कज्जलं च प्रसूयते ।
en: A lamp eats darkness and gives out soot; in the same way, the kind of food one always eats shapes the children one has.

first: वित्तंदेहि गुणान्वितेष मतिमन्नाऽन्यत्रदेहि क्वचित् ।
en: Wise one, give your wealth to the worthy and to no one else. The sea water that clouds take up turns sweet; it gives life to all things on earth, moving and still, and returns to the sea many millions of times greater.

first: चाण्डालानां सहस्त्रैश्च सूरिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ।
en: Wise men who see the truth say that one Yavana is as low as a thousand outcasts; there is no one lower than a Yavana.

first: तैलाभ्यड्गे चिताधूमे मैथुने क्षौरकर्मणि ।
en: After an oil rub, after touching smoke from a funeral pyre, after sex, and after a shave, a person stays unclean until he bathes.

first: अजीर्णे भेषजं वारि जार्णे वारि बलप्रदम् ।
en: Water is medicine when food is not digested, it gives strength once food is digested, it is like nectar during a meal, and like poison right after it.

first: हतं ज्ञानं क्रियाहीनं हतश्चाऽज्ञानतो नरः ।
en: Knowledge without action is wasted, a man is ruined by ignorance, an army without a leader is lost, and women without husbands are lost.

first: वृध्द्काले मृता भार्या बन्धुहस्ते गतं धनम् ।
en: A wife dying in old age, wealth falling into the hands of relatives, and depending on others for food: these three are a man's misfortunes.

first: अग्निहोत्रं विना वेदाः न च दानं विना क्रियाः ।
en: The Vedas are nothing without the fire offering, and rites are nothing without gifts; nothing succeeds without true feeling, so feeling is what matters.

first: न देवो विद्यते काष्ठे न पाषाणे न मृण्मये ।
en: God is not in wood, nor in stone, nor in clay; God is found in true feeling, so feeling is what matters.

first: काष्ठ-पाषाण-धातूनां कृत्वा भावेन सेवनम् ।
en: When one worships images of wood, stone or metal with true feeling and faith, success comes by the grace of Vishnu.

first: शान्तितुल्यं तपो नास्ति न सन्तोषात्परं सुखम् ।
en: There is no penance equal to calmness, no happiness greater than contentment, no disease worse than craving, and no duty higher than compassion.

first: क्रोधो वैवस्वतो राहा तृष्णा वैतरणी नदी ।
en: Anger is like the god of death, craving is like the river of hell, learning is like the wish-granting cow, and contentment is like the garden of heaven.

first: गुणो भूषयते रूपं शीलं भूषयते कुलम् ।
en: Good qualities adorn beauty, good conduct adorns a family, success adorns learning, and enjoying it adorns wealth.

first: निर्गुणस्य हतं रूपं दुःशीलस्य हतं कुलम् ।
en: Beauty is wasted in one without good qualities, a family is spoiled by bad conduct, learning is wasted without success, and wealth is wasted if it is not enjoyed.

first: शुद्धं भूमिगतं तोयं शुद्धा नारी पतिव्रता ।
en: Water that has sunk into the ground is pure, a faithful wife is pure, a king who brings welfare is pure, and a contented Brahmin is pure.

first: असंतुष्टा द्विजा नष्टाः संतुष्टाश् च महीभृतः ।
en: A discontented Brahmin is ruined, a contented king is ruined, a shy courtesan is ruined, and a shameless woman of good family is ruined.

first: किं कुलेन विशालेन विद्याहीनेन देहिनाम् ।
en: What use is a great family if a person has no learning? A learned person, even from a low family, is honoured even by the gods.

first: विद्वान् प्रशस्यते लोके विद्वान्सर्वत्र गौरवम् ।
en: A learned person is praised in the world and respected everywhere; through learning one gains everything, and learning is honoured everywhere.

first: रूपयौवनसंपन्ना विशालकुलसम्भवाः ।
en: Even those who have beauty, youth and a great family do not shine without learning, like kinshuk flowers that have no scent.

first: मांसभक्षैः सुरापानैः मूर्खैश्चाऽक्षरवर्जितैः ।
en: The earth is weighed down by beasts in human form: meat-eaters, drunkards, and fools who cannot even read.

first: अन्नहीना दहेद्राष्ट्रं मंत्रहीनश्च रिषीत्विजः ।
en: A sacrifice where no food is given burns the kingdom, one without proper chants burns the priests, and one without gifts burns the patron; no enemy is like such a sacrifice.
